chapter.title: Industrial Networks
chapter.prerequisites: Chapter 1, especially 1.7 The Industrial Robot Cell; 2.5 End-of-Arm Tooling and I/O; 4.4 Making a Robot Cell Safe. Python for the labs in 8.3 and 8.6.
chapter.handsOn: write and read Modbus TCP registers on a stand-in robot server with Python and pymodbus, and capture and decode that traffic in Wireshark; no hardware needed.
chapter.summary: Sinking and sourcing I/O and the move from wiring to fieldbuses and Ethernet, industrial Ethernet protocols (EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, EtherCAT, Modbus TCP), a robot-to-PLC Modbus lab, safety protocols and the black channel principle, IO-Link, OPC UA, MQTT and ros2_control, and network security, TSN and Wireshark diagnostics.

lessons.title: From Wires to Networks
objectives: Compare sinking and sourcing DC circuits, evaluating how NPN and PNP 3-wire field devices interface with PLC I/O modules.
Explain how fieldbuses replaced point-to-point wiring and analyze how industrial Ethernet supports multiple protocols on shared media.
Differentiate cyclic I/O data exchange from acyclic diagnostic messaging between controllers and field devices.
Evaluate line, star, and ring physical topologies, examining recovery times and node limits in Device Level Ring networks.

lessons.title: Industrial Ethernet Protocols
objectives: Explain how EtherNet/IP combines standard Ethernet with CIP, contrasting implicit UDP messaging with explicit TCP messaging.
Analyze PROFINET RT and IRT communication mechanisms, device hierarchy models, and the 50 percent bandwidth reservation rule.
Describe how EtherCAT processes frames on the fly using EtherType 0x88A4, dedicated slave controllers, and distributed clocks.
Interpret XML-based device description files (GSDML, ESI) and examine the Modbus TCP register model and MBAP header.

lessons.title: Lab: Connecting a Robot to a PLC
objectives: Describe how a Universal Robots controller connects to a PLC over EtherNet/IP, PROFINET and Modbus TCP.
Locate the general-purpose registers (128 to 255) of the UR Modbus TCP server and pack up to 16 handshake bits into one register with URScript.
Write and read holding registers from Python with the pymodbus ModbusTcpClient against a stand-in server.
Read a Modbus exception response: the function code plus 0x80 and exception code 02 (ILLEGAL DATA ADDRESS).

lessons.title: Safety over the Network
objectives: Explain the black channel principle and how safety communication operates over unverified transmission media.
Compare functional safety standards across PROFIsafe (IEC 61784-3-3), FailSafe over EtherCAT (IEC 61784-3), and CIP Safety.
Describe how CIP Safety verifies data transfer integrity using timestamps, production identifiers, and Safety Network Numbers.
Describe the safety signals a robot and a safety PLC exchange over PROFIsafe and which stop category each one triggers.

lessons.title: From the Plant Floor to IT
objectives: Characterize point-to-point IO-Link sensor communication under IEC 61131-9, baud rates, and IODD device descriptions.
Explain the OPC UA architecture under IEC 62541, binary TCP transport over port 4840, and X.509v3 PKI security.
Explain what the VDMA 40010 OPC UA Robotics companion specification standardizes.
Explain MQTT publish/subscribe and its three Quality of Service levels, and how ros2_control's Controller Manager runs the control loop.

lessons.title: Network Design, Security and Diagnostics
objectives: Apply the ISA/IEC 62443 standard framework, shared stakeholder responsibility, and security zones and conduits.
Structure industrial demilitarized zones (DMZs) with push and pull data boundaries and multifactor authentication jump boxes.
Explain how VLANs, static access ports and a dedicated management VLAN protect a managed switch.
Capture Modbus traffic in Wireshark using the loopback interface, Decode As and the mbtcp and modbus display filters, and name the main TSN standards.

blurbs.8-1: From discrete wiring to industrial networks: sinking and sourcing (NPN/PNP), fieldbus history, line, star and ring topologies, cyclic versus acyclic data, and Device Level Ring recovery.
blurbs.8-2: Industrial Ethernet protocols: EtherNet/IP CIP implicit and explicit messaging, PROFINET RT and IRT with GSDML, EtherCAT on-the-fly frame processing with ESI, and Modbus TCP.
blurbs.8-3: Lab: the UR Modbus TCP server and its general-purpose registers, packing handshake bits in URScript, and writing and reading registers from Python with pymodbus (stand-in server, no hardware).
blurbs.8-4: Functional safety over industrial networks: the black channel principle, PROFIsafe, FailSafe over EtherCAT (FSoE), CIP Safety, and stop category classifications.
blurbs.8-5: Integrating plant-floor devices with enterprise IT: IO-Link sensor architecture, OPC UA information modeling and the VDMA 40010 robotics specification, MQTT telemetry, and ros2_control.
blurbs.8-6: Network design, security and diagnostics: ISA/IEC 62443, zones and the DMZ, VLANs, Time-Sensitive Networking, and a Wireshark lab that decodes the 8.3 Modbus traffic.

glossary.acyclic communication: Communication that transmits diagnostic data on an as-needed basis rather than adhering to a fixed cyclic update schedule.
glossary.black channel principle: A functional safety networking design where safety and standard communication integrate on one transmission medium by treating the underlying network as unreliable and placing diagnostics entirely in end devices.
glossary.CIP Safety: A functional safety protocol enabling standard and safety devices to operate together on the same network using time-stamped data and production identifiers.
glossary.Controller Manager: A component in the ros2_control framework that connects controllers with the hardware abstraction interface.
glossary.cyclic communication: Regular data transmission where inputs and outputs are transferred between a controller and I/O devices at a defined update cycle time.
glossary.demilitarized zone: A physical and logical subnet acting as an intermediary between corporate and control networks so connected devices avoid direct exposure to untrusted networks.
glossary.Device Level Ring: An industrial Ethernet ring topology featuring an active ring supervisor transmitting beacon frames, achieving a worst-case recovery time of 2890 µs on copper with default beacon settings.
glossary.EtherCAT: An industrial Ethernet technology where slave devices with dedicated EtherCAT Slave Controllers read and insert data on the fly as standard frames with EtherType 0x88A4 pass downstream.
glossary.EtherNet/IP: An industrial automation communication network combining standard Ethernet and TCP/IP technologies with the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP).
glossary.exception response: A Modbus error message returned by a server using the request function code plus 0x80 when a request cannot be executed.
glossary.explicit messaging: Request-reply client-server transactions in EtherNet/IP that use TCP and are addressed to the Message Router object.
glossary.FailSafe over EtherCAT: An EtherCAT functional safety protocol (FSoE) standardized in IEC 61784-3 that embeds safety containers within cyclical process data.
glossary.fieldbus: A digital communication technology that served as a replacement for point-to-point wiring when connecting sensors and field devices to PLCs.
glossary.GSDML: An XML-based device description language compliant with ISO 15745 used to define the properties of PROFINET field devices.
glossary.holding register: A 16-bit Modbus data storage register accessed using function code 0x03 to read or function codes 0x06 and 0x10 to write.
glossary.IEEE 802.1AS: A Layer 2 timing and synchronization standard for time-sensitive applications specified as a profile of IEEE 1588.
glossary.ILLEGAL DATA ADDRESS: Modbus exception code 02 indicating that the register address received in the request is not allowed for the server.
glossary.implicit messaging: Time-critical connected communications in EtherNet/IP that transport I/O data using UDP without embedded protocol headers.
glossary.integer_to_binary_list: A URScript command that converts an integer into a little-endian list of boolean values where the first element is the least significant bit.
glossary.IO-Link: A globally standardized point-to-point IO technology under IEC 61131-9 for communicating with sensors and actuators using standard three-wire cables and M12, M8, or M5 connectors.
glossary.ISA/IEC 62443: A horizontal international standard series defining requirements and processes for implementing and maintaining secure industrial automation and control systems.
glossary.mbtcp: The Wireshark display filter protocol name for Modbus/TCP, defining fields including Transaction Identifier, Protocol Identifier, and Length.
glossary.ModbusTcpClient: A pymodbus client class that connects to a target Modbus TCP device over socket framing on default port 502.
glossary.MQTT: A lightweight client-server publish/subscribe messaging transport protocol requiring an ordered, lossless stream of bytes over TCP ports 1883 or 8883.
glossary.OPC UA: An open platform-independent communication architecture standardized in IEC 62541 using TCP port 4840, PKI with X.509v3 certificates, and hierarchical address spaces.
glossary.PROFINET RT: A PROFINET communication class that bypasses TCP/IP layers to achieve deterministic communication in the 1 to 10 millisecond range.
glossary.PROFIsafe: A functional safety communication standard under IEC 61784-3-3 complying with SIL 3 under IEC 61508 and PL e category 4 under ISO 13849.
glossary.Quality of Service: Message delivery guarantees defined in MQTT consisting of three levels: At most once, At least once, and Exactly once.
glossary.read_port_register: A URScript command that reads a controller register and returns an integer value between 0 and 65535.
glossary.Safety Network Number: A unique identifier in CIP Safety that identifies each network path individually to allow each device to be uniquely identified.
glossary.sinking: A DC circuit configuration providing a path to supply common (-).
glossary.sourcing: A DC circuit configuration providing a path to supply source (+).
glossary.Time-Sensitive Networking: An IEEE 802 standards family designed to provide deterministic connectivity with bounded latency, low packet delay variation, and low packet loss.
glossary.VDMA 40010: The OPC UA Companion Specification for Robotics defining a standardized information model for asset management, condition monitoring, and preventive maintenance across robot brands.
glossary.VLAN: A virtual local area network that divides physical switches into smaller logical broadcast domains to isolate network traffic.
glossary.F-device: A fail-safe device in PROFIsafe; implementing the PROFIsafe protocol alone cannot turn a standard device into one, because its safety level depends on its safety hardware architecture.

quiz.question: Which type of PLC input module is required when connecting an NPN sinking field device?
quiz.explanation: An NPN sinking field device requires a PLC I/O module with a sourcing input.

quiz.question: What maximum node count does Rockwell Automation recommend for a Device Level Ring network to avoid degraded recovery time and network performance?
quiz.explanation: Rockwell Automation recommends limiting a Device Level Ring network to 50 or fewer nodes to avoid degraded recovery time and network performance.

quiz.question: How are time-critical I/O data transported in EtherNet/IP implicit messaging?
choices: Using TCP addressed to the Message Router object
Using UDP without embedded protocol headers
quiz.explanation: Implicit messages in EtherNet/IP are time-critical connected communications that transport I/O data using UDP without embedded protocol headers.

quiz.question: Which EtherType value identifies EtherCAT frames within standard Ethernet frames?
quiz.explanation: EtherCAT frames are identified by EtherType 0x88A4 in standard Ethernet frames, eliminating the overhead of TCP/IP or UDP/IP stacks.

quiz.question: Which address range provides 128 general-purpose 16-bit registers on the Universal Robots Modbus TCP server?
quiz.explanation: The Universal Robots Modbus TCP server provides 128 general-purpose 16-bit registers at addresses 128 to 255.

quiz.question: When a Modbus server returns an exception response because it cannot carry out a request, how is the exception function code calculated?
quiz.explanation: When a Modbus server cannot carry out a request, its exception response uses the request function code plus 0x80.

quiz.question: What premise defines the black channel principle in functional safety communication?
choices: All network switches must perform hardware-level encryption on safety packets
Safety signals must be transmitted exclusively over dedicated fiber optic cables
The transmission network is unreliable, meaning safety diagnostics must exist outside the network infrastructure
The network layer must guarantee zero packet loss under all operating conditions
quiz.explanation: The black channel principle assumes the network is unreliable, meaning diagnostics must exist outside the network infrastructure.

quiz.question: What action occurs when an emergency stop triggers a Stop Category 1 over PROFIsafe?
choices: Drive power is removed immediately without controlled deceleration
The robot stops motion while drive power remains continuously on
The robot executes a reverse trajectory along the programmed path
A controlled stop commands motion to stop before removing power
quiz.explanation: An emergency stop over PROFIsafe triggers a Stop Category 1 controlled stop that commands motion to stop before removing power.

quiz.question: Which IANA registered port is used for optimized binary OPC UA Client-Server communications over TCP?
quiz.explanation: OPC UA Client-Server communications use an optimized TCP-based binary protocol for data exchange over IANA registered port 4840.

quiz.question: Which VDMA specification number designates the OPC UA Companion Specification for Robotics?
quiz.explanation: The OPC UA Robotics companion specification was released as VDMA Specification number 40010.

quiz.question: How do secure industrial DMZ communication architectures handle data movement between control zones and enterprise users?
choices: Control zones push data to the DMZ and enterprise users pull data from DMZ application servers
Enterprise users pull data directly from Level 1 controller LANs
Control zones pull configuration files directly from public enterprise cloud services
Enterprise users push commands straight through the DMZ to Level 0 field devices
quiz.explanation: Secure DMZ communication models require control zones to push data to the DMZ and enterprise users to pull data from DMZ application servers.

quiz.question: In Wireshark, which display filter protocol name provides fields such as Transaction Identifier, Protocol Identifier, and Length?
quiz.explanation: In Wireshark, the Modbus/TCP display filter protocol name is mbtcp, which defines fields including Transaction Identifier, Protocol Identifier, and Length.
